title: Grateful Dead Live at Hartford Civic Center on 1982-04-17
lineage: Aud > mastercassette > DAT > CDR > EAC > Flac-level8
source: FOB-Nak 700's > Sony D5  recorded by Barry Glassberg

ai_review.summary: Hand‑held audience FOB captures a high‑energy 1982 show with a monster Shakedown Street, blazing Spanish Jam and standout Uncle John's Band/Not Fade Away sequence.
ai_review.review: The recording, taken from a well‑placed hand‑held FOB, delivers strong punch and enough clarity to hear the band’s dynamics, even if Phil’s bass sits low in the mix. Musically the show shines on the second set – Shakedown Street rolls into an epic Spanish Jam, followed by Space, Uncle John's Band, Not Fade Away and a soaring Wharf Rat/​Baby Blue finish – while the first set is solid but less memorable. Overall fans rave about the band’s enthusiasm and tight interplay, making this a must‑listen for 1982 Deadheads.

ai_rating.rationale: Consistently high praise for both performance (standout jams, high energy) and recording quality (hand‑held FOB with strong punch), offset only by minor mix issues.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Hand‑held FOB captures good punch and overall clarity; some reviewers note Phil’s bass is low in the mix but no major dropouts or distortion reported.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set solid but middle‑of‑the‑road; second set ignites with Shakedown Street and a marathon Spanish Jam, flowing smoothly into Space, Uncle John's Band and a powerful Not Fade Away/Wharf Rat finish.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for clean tone, crisp plucking/plunking, strong vocal delivery and memorable Robbie Robertson‑style licks; drives the jams with sweet lines throughout.
band_member_comments.Phil: Bass noted as low in the mix on this recording but still provides a solid foundation; occasional “bomb” moments mentioned.
band_member_comments.Bob: Vocals described as great and full of feeling; leads Lost Sailor segment with nice reading, blends well with Brent on vocal harmonies.
band_member_comments.Keys: Brent Mydland receives multiple accolades – piano solo in the Spanish Jam, standout piano sound on Uncle John's Band, and overall strong keyboard contribution.
band_member_comments.Drums: The drummers keep a steady groove that underpins the jams; no specific complaints, just noted for holding the rhythm tight.
